title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page belongs to the 1976 IHÉS lecture notes on the divided-power de Rham complex. In the surrounding pages Grothendieck asks when a functor F between categories of modules or complexes carries divided-power (PD) structures to PD structures. The previous and next pages build a map u_p^X : Γ^p F(X) → F(Γ^p X), x ↦ x^{(p)}, using the monoidality of F, and check the PD axioms for these induced x^{(p)}.

This page has three parts.

(1) Opening questions, partly illegible. Grothendieck considers a natural 'degree p' operation F(J) → P(J), a polynomial law induced by γ^p : J → J. He asks whether, for x, y ∈ F(J), the induced operation satisfies the additivity formula (x+y)^{(p)} = Σ_{i+j=p} x^{(i)} y^{(j)}. He requires that F : P → P' commute with tensor products and be compatible with degrees and partial degrees ('bidegrés 1,1'). In modern terms F is a lax symmetric monoidal functor, for example a normalization or Eilenberg–Zilber type functor.

(2) A careful axiomatic definition of a PD-algebra in non-unital form:
- A is a commutative associative ring with 1 (with a ring map k → Hom(O, A)).
- J is a commutative associative algebra without 1 on which A acts, with (λx)y = x(λy) = λ(xy).
- i : J → A is a homomorphism of A-algebras.
- There are maps γ^p : J → J of degree p for p ≥ 1, with γ^0 = 1 : J → A and γ^1 = id_J.
- γ^p(x+y) = Σ_{i+j=p} γ^i(x) γ^j(y).
- γ^p(λx) = λ^p γ^p(x).
- γ^p(x) γ^q(x) = C(p+q, p) γ^{p+q}(x).
- γ^p(γ^q(x)) = (pq)!/((p!)^q q!) γ^{pq}(x).
This is essentially the Cartan/Roby definition of an ideal with divided powers, with J an abstract non-unital algebra rather than an ideal (Berthelot's set-up).

(3) The final line, after a heading roughly 'transformation induite ...', introduces the natural map Γ^* F(X) → F Γ^*(X) from the divided-power algebra on F(X) to F of the divided-power algebra on X. The next page develops it: it is a map of graded algebras, and the question is whether F Γ^*(X) is again a PD-algebra.

Overall purpose: to transport PD structures through tensor-compatible functors. The aim is presumably to put divided powers on the de Rham complex of a PD-algebra, or on (co)homology or normalized complexes, in the manner of Cartan's divided powers on the homotopy of simplicial commutative rings.
errors: The axiom list omits γ^p(xy) = i(x)^p γ^p(y) for x, y ∈ J (equivalently γ^p(ax) = a^p γ^p(x) for a ∈ i(J)). In the non-unital set-up this is not covered by the scalar axiom γ^p(λx) = λ^p γ^p(x) for λ ∈ A. It is a standard axiom (Roby, Berthelot), so this is a gap in the definition, perhaps intended implicitly.
The compatibility of i with the γ's, and the consequence p! γ^p(x) = x^p in J, are not stated.
The '(deg p)!' formula in the opening query is ambiguous as written. The intended identity is presumably the plain additivity formula Σ_{i+j=p} x^{(i)} y^{(j)}, not one multiplied by a factorial.

ideas.what: Axiomatic definition of a PD-structure on a non-unital commutative A-algebra J with structure map i : J → A
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Cartan (1954–55 seminar), N. Roby (1963–65), P. Berthelot (1974)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck discussed PD structures in the crystalline context (e.g. 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', 1966/68); this exact axiomatization is not recalled there

ideas.what: Natural transformation Γ^* F(X) → F(Γ^* X) for a tensor-compatible functor F, used to induce divided powers x^{(p)} on F(X) and to check the PD axioms
ideas.modern_name: Transport of divided powers along a lax symmetric monoidal functor (e.g. Eilenberg–Zilber / Dold–Kan; divided powers on homotopy of simplicial commutative rings)
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Cartan (Séminaire Cartan 1954–55); later Illusie (Complexe cotangent), Fresse, and others

ideas.what: Using the degree-p map induced by γ^p as a polynomial law F(J) → P(J)
ideas.modern_name: Polynomial laws / polynomial functors (Roby); strict polynomial functors
ideas.usually_credited_to: N. Roby (1963); Friedlander–Suslin (1997) for strict polynomial functors

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a general criterion: a functor F compatible with tensor products and bidegrees should carry PD-structures to PD-structures via Γ^* F → F Γ^*. The question of whether F Γ^*(X) is itself a PD-algebra is left open on the next page. This is a functorial framework close to later operadic treatments of divided powers (Fresse's Γ(P, -)), but it is only a sketch and is largely covered by Cartan's and later work.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's 1976 approach to divided powers on de Rham complexes through a monoidal-functor formalism. This is of historical interest, but it is unlikely to contain mathematics unknown to specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: The page mostly writes out standard PD axioms and starts a routine transport-of-structure argument. Its only interest is as unpublished evidence of Grothendieck's functorial approach in the 1976 lecture.
transcription_corrections: 'Γ^× F(X) → F Γ^×(X)' should read Γ^* F(X) → F Γ^*(X), as on the next page.
'k → Hom(O, A)' could be read as k → Hom(O, A) or k → Hom(1, A); the 'O' is uncertain.
The line before the last formula appears to read 'transformation induite ...' (heading for the map Γ^* F → F Γ^*).
'J →i A hom de A-[?]' should probably read 'hom de A-algèbres' (an A-algebra map, given i(xy) = i(x)i(y) and i(λx) = λ i(x)).
'A ⊗ J → J' could be read as A ⊗ J → J or A × J → J (the A-module structure on J).
The note at the right of the middle section reads 'bidegrés 1,1'.
The words under P →F P' appear to be 'commute aux produits tensoriels' (struck through) and 'compatible aux degrés et degrés partiels'.
